title: Review: Combustion and fuels; Hess's law cycles; Bond enthalpies; Collision theory and factors
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN03#t2 term and clue written for the game; KN02#t1 term and clue written for the game; EN03#t1 term and clue written for the game; KN02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN03#N.10a, EN04#N.10, EN11#N.15, KN02#N.9b, EN04#N.9a, EN11#N.5, KN02#N.7a, EN11#N.3, KN02#N.2a, EN11#N.8, KN02#N.4a, EN11#N.14. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Endothermic
items.clue: Describes the breaking of a bond: energy is absorbed.

items.label: Collision theory
items.clue: The idea that particles must hit each other, with enough energy, in order to react.

items.label: Bond enthalpy
items.clue: Energy needed to break 1 mol of one type of link between atoms, all species gaseous.

items.label: Activation energy
items.clue: The minimum that an impact between particles must have for them to react, symbol Ea.

questions.stem: CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₃Cl(g) + HCl(g), ΔH = −99 kJ mol⁻¹. Bond enthalpies / kJ mol⁻¹: C–H 413, Cl–Cl 243, H–Cl 432. What value for the C–Cl bond enthalpy do these data give?

options.text: 125 kJ mol⁻¹
755 kJ mol⁻¹
323 kJ mol⁻¹
162 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: One C–H and one Cl–Cl break (656 kJ); one C–Cl and one H–Cl form. 656 − (x + 432) = −99, so x = 323 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Graphite turns into diamond only at enormous pressures, so ΔH for C(s, graphite) → C(s, diamond) can't be measured directly. But both forms burn. (1) C(s, graphite) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −393.5 kJ mol⁻¹ · (2) C(s, diamond) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), ΔH = −395.4 kJ mol⁻¹. What is ΔH for graphite → diamond?

options.text: ΔH = +1.9 kJ mol⁻¹
ΔH = −1.9 kJ mol⁻¹
ΔH = −788.9 kJ mol⁻¹
ΔH = +788.9 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: Keep (1); reverse (2), so its ΔH becomes +395.4. Add: CO₂ and O₂ cancel. ΔH = −393.5 + 395.4 = +1.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: After cooking outdoors, campers carry a still-glowing charcoal barbecue into their closed tent for warmth. Charcoal is almost pure carbon. Why is this deadly, even though there is no flame?

options.text: The charcoal burns to extra carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, which binds to haemoglobin in place of oxygen.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, an acidic gas that damages the lungs.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, which binds to haemoglobin.
The charcoal uses up all of the oxygen in the tent, and this lack of oxygen suffocates the campers.

questions.stem: A glowing splint only smoulders in air, but bursts into flame when it is lowered into a gas jar of pure oxygen at the same temperature and pressure. Air is about 21% oxygen. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Molecules of pure oxygen have more kinetic energy, so their collisions with the wood are more energetic.
Each unit volume holds about five times as many O₂ molecules, so collisions with the wood are far more frequent.
Pure oxygen acts as a catalyst, giving a route with a lower activation energy for the burning of wood.
Pure oxygen contains no nitrogen, so each mole of O₂ that reacts with the wood releases more energy.

questions.stem: Use the enthalpy changes of reactions 1 and 2 to calculate ΔH for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide: 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). Reaction 1: H₂(g) + O₂(g) → H₂O₂(l), ΔH₁ = −187.8 kJ mol⁻¹. Reaction 2: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l), ΔH₂ = −571.6 kJ mol⁻¹.

options.text: −947.2 kJ mol⁻¹
+196.0 kJ mol⁻¹
−383.8 kJ mol⁻¹
−196.0 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: Reverse and double reaction 1: +375.6. Add reaction 2: −571.6. 2H₂ and one O₂ cancel. ΔH = −196.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, O₂, is needed to burn 0.500 mol of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH, completely?

options.text: 2.25 mol
2.50 mol
4.50 mol
1.25 mol

questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH + 4½O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 10 O atoms; the alcohol supplies 1, so O₂ supplies 9: 4½ O₂ per mole. 0.500 × 4.5 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: Which statement explains how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction at constant temperature?

options.text: It gives the reacting particles more kinetic energy, so more collisions exceed Ea.
It increases the concentration of the reactants, so collisions happen more often.
It makes the reaction more exothermic, so more energy is available for collisions.
It provides a route with a lower Ea, so a larger fraction of collisions have enough energy.

questions.explanation: Same particles, same energies, but a lower barrier. More collisions now have E ≥ Ea, so more succeed each second.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed.

questions.stem: In a mixture of two gases at room temperature, each molecule collides with others billions of times every second, yet the reaction between them is slow. Why do most of these collisions not lead to a reaction?

options.text: Most collisions have less energy than ΔH, the energy that the reaction gives out.
Most collisions have less energy than Ea, the minimum needed for a reaction.
A catalyst must be present in each collision before any bonds can break.
Most of the molecules are moving far too slowly to collide with one another.

questions.explanation: Only collisions with energy of at least Ea lead to reaction. At room temperature that is a tiny fraction, so the reaction is slow.

questions.stem: Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of ethanol?

options.text: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + 1½O₂(g) → 2C(s) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + 4O(g) → 2CO(g) + 3H₂O(l)
C₂H₅OH(l) + O₂(g) → 2C(s) + 3H₂O(l)

questions.explanation: In very limited O₂ the carbon is deposited as soot while the hydrogen still forms water. 3 O atoms in the products: 1 from ethanol, 2 from O₂.

questions.stem: Hydrogen iodide decomposes: 2HI(g) → H₂(g) + I₂(g). A sample of hydrogen iodide is compressed to half its volume at constant temperature. What is the effect on the rate of reaction, and why?

options.text: It is unchanged: there are equal amounts of gas on both sides of the equation, so pressure has no effect.
It increases: the compressed molecules collide more energetically, so more collisions exceed Ea.
It increases: a larger amount of H₂ and I₂ can now form from the same amount of HI as before.
It increases: collisions become more frequent, and the fraction with E ≥ Ea is unchanged.

questions.stem: Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugar from sugar cane and is burned as a fuel for vehicles. Which statement about bioethanol as a fuel is correct?

options.text: It burns to form water only, so using it as a fuel adds no CO₂ to the atmosphere.
The CO₂ it releases is exactly balanced by photosynthesis, so its net emission is zero.
All of its carbon was fixed from atmospheric CO₂ by photosynthesis in the cane.
Its carbon was taken from the soil by the roots of the cane, not from CO₂ in the air.

questions.explanation: The cane took its carbon from the air within the last year or two. Even so, fossil fuels used to grow and process it add CO₂, so it is not carbon neutral.
